chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masrouq, from Yazeed ibn Ishaq Shairin, from Al-Husayn ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The noble character traits are ten. So if you have the capacity for them to be in you, let them be, for they may be in a man and not in his son, and in the son and not in his father, and in the slave and not in the free man. It was said, 'And what are they?' He said: 'Truthfulness in bravery, truthfulness of the tongue, fulfilling the trust, maintaining kinship, honoring the guest, feeding the beggar, repaying good deeds, being considerate to the neighbor, being considerate to the companion, and the head of them all is bashfulness (modesty).'
ai.seo_question: What are the ten noble character traits (makarim al-akhlaq) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines *al-makarim* (noble character traits) as ten specific virtues that are acquired through spiritual effort rather than inherited, emphasizing their independence from lineage or social status. The list culminates in *al-hayaa'* (modesty/shyness) as the root of all nobilities, a concept deeply valued in Shia ethics as the guardian of other virtues. This enumeration serves as a practical guide for moral self-cultivation (*akhlaq*), linking internal character to external social conduct.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Haysam Bin Abu Masrouq, from Yazeed Bin Is’haq Shairin, from Al Husayn Bin Atiyya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The nobilities are ten. So if you have the capacity that they should happen to be in you, so let it happen, for these can happen to be in the man and not happen to be in his son, and these can happen to be in the son and not happen to be in his father, and these can happen to be in the slave and not happen to be in the free (one)’. It was said, ‘And what are these?’ 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘True bravery, and truthful of the tongue, and paying the entrustments, and helping the relatives, and entertaining the guest, and feeding the beggar, and the rewarding upon the works, and the responsibility for the neighbour, and the responsibility for the companions – and the head of these is ‘الْحَيَاءُ’ the bashfulness’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hatham ibn abu Masruq from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha’ar from al-Husayn ibn al- ‘Atiyah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Noble (human) qualities are ten. If you can establish all of them so be it. Such qualities may be found in a man but may not be found in his children. They may be found in the children but not in the father. At times they are found in a slave person but not in a free one.’ It was asked, ‘What are these noble qualities?’ The Imam said they are: ‘Losing all hope in the true sense for receiving help from anyone other than Allah, truthfulness of tongue, returning the trust (safely), maintaining good relations with relatives, entertaining guests, feeding the needy, making up for favors in a proper corresponding manner, keeping up with one’s responsibilities toward the neighbors and with one’s companion, and the head of such qualities is bashfulness.’”
